well-architect.redologs-placement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends placing redo logs, whether multiplexed or not, on a dedicated volume or shared with temp/control files to isolate their high-write I/O from data file transactions, improving performance. Each multiplexed redo log copy should reside on a separate volume for redundancy. Frequent changes make redo logs unsuitable for snapshotted volumes, like data volumes, as they inflate snapshot sizes. Redo logs must not be placed on volumes tiered to object storage, such as archive volumes, as their frequent updates are incompatible with object storage's slower access patterns. This separation enables customized efficiency mechanisms and tiering configurations for optimal database performance and cost efficiency.
well-architect.redologs-placement-optimization-step1: Create a new dedicated volume (or ASM disk group) for logs and connect it to the server
well-architect.temp-placement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends placing temp files on a dedicated volume or with redo/control files to isolate their high-write I/O from data files, improving performance. Temp tablespaces change frequently but don’t require restoration, so it's best to avoid placing them on snapshotted volumes, such as data volumes, to prevent bloated snapshots. Temp files must not be placed on volumes tiered to object storage, such as archive volumes, as their frequent updates can degrade database performance.
well-architect.data-log-separation-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends separating data and log files onto different drives to improve performance and functionality.
well-architect.data-log-separation-benefit1: Separating data and log files onto different drives improves performance by allowing simultaneous I/O activity, independent backup schedules, and improved restore functionality.
well-architect.data-log-separation-recommendation1: We recommend separating data and log LUN paths into different volumes for smaller databases.
well-architect.data-log-separation-requirement1: This separation is required when there is more than one large database (> 500 GiB).
well-architect.oracle-storagelayout-note1: It is crucial that you schedule this task during maintenance window to minimize disruptions to your operations. This process could involve data loss and downtime. To prepare, perform necessary backups and notify all affected users to avoid any unintended downtime or data loss.
well-architect.archive-placement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends placing archive logs on a dedicated volume to ensure efficient backup and recovery processes and reduce storage cost. By separating archive logs, you can apply specific storage configurations, such as compression and tiering policies, to optimize cost and performance. This separation also facilitates efficient snapshot and backup strategies, ensuring that archive logs are readily available for recovery without impacting the performance of redo logs, data files, or control files.
well-architect.datafile-placement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends placing data files on a dedicated volume or shared with control files to boost performance by isolating their random I/O from redo or archive log writes. This separation allows you to benefit from customized snapshot configurations, tiering policies, and efficiency mechanisms to optimize performance and cost.
well-architect.controlfile-placement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends multiplexing control files to avoid a single point of failure in production environments. Maintain at least two, preferably three, control file copies across separate volumes or disks to enhance redundancy and reduce the risk of losing all copies. Control files can be placed on a dedicated volume or shared with redo logs or data files, but avoid placing them on volumes tiered to object storage, such as archive volumes, as its slower access pattern is incompatible with control file performance needs.
well-architect.oracle-binary-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends placing Oracle binaries on a dedicated volume to ensure optimal performance and stability by reducing I/O contention with other files. This separation simplifies software updates and minimizes the risk of accidental modifications or corruption, ensuring the database runs smoothly.

well-architect.oracle-thin-provisioning-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends configuring thin provisioning for FSx for ONTAP volumes hosting Oracle databases. This approach optimizes storage efficiency and cost-effectiveness by allowing more logical data to be stored than physically available.
well-architect.oracle-thin-provisioning-what-will-happe: Workload Factory will enable thin provisioning on the selected volumes.
well-architect.oracle-autosize-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling volume autogrow for FSx for ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility, availability, and scalability for Oracle databases by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth, preventing space shortages and avoiding downtime if a volume runs out of space. Volume autogrow is essential when enabling thin provisioning.
well-architect.oracle-autosize-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will enable volume autogrow on the selected volumes.
well-architect.oracle-autosize-mode-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling autosize for FSx ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. This configuration enhances flexibility and availability by allowing volumes to grow dynamically to accommodate unexpected data growth. This prevents space shortages and helps avoid downtime if a volume runs out of space, ensuring seamless scalability for Oracle databases. Volume autogrow is essential when enabling thin provisioning.
well-architect.oracle-autosize-mode-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will enable autosize on the selected volumes and Autosize mode will be set to grow.
well-architect.oracle-fractional-reserve-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends disabling fractional reserve to eliminate unnecessary space reservation for overwrites thereby optimizing space utilization and cost-effectiveness for thin-provisioned FSx for ONTAP volumes. This configuration is essential when using thin provisioning with Oracle databases.
well-architect.oracle-fractional-reserve-what-will-happ: Workload Factory will set the fractional reserve to 0% on the selected volumes.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-policy-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends disabling the native ONTAP snapshots for FSx ONTAP volumes for Oracle databases. Oracle snapshots should be managed externally via tools like SnapCenter, which creates application-consistent snapshots, preventing corruption during restoration.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-policy-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will disable the snapshot policy on the selected volumes.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-copy-reserve-action-summ: Workload Factory recommends that capacity isn't reserved for snapshots on FSx for ONTAP volumes used by databases, making the entire volume capacity available for active data and any snapshots that are created.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-copy-reserve-what-will-h: Workload Factory will set the snapshot copy reserve to 0% on the selected  volumes.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-autodelete-action-summar: Workload Factory recommends configuring the snapshot autodelete feature in FSx for ONTAP for Oracle databases to delete older snapshots first. This feature is designed to automatically manage snapshot storage by deleting the oldest snapshots when a volume approaches its capacity limit. This configuration helps in thin-provisioned environments, where more logical storage is allocated than physically available.
well-architect.oracle-snapshot-autodelete-what-will-hap: Workload Factory will configure snapshot autodelete to delete the oldest snapshot first on the selected volumes.
well-architect.oracle-space-mgmt-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends configuring space management to prioritize volume expansion over snapshot deletion for thin-provisioned FSx for ONTAP volumes with volume autogrow enabled.
well-architect.oracle-space-mgmt-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will configure space management to prioritize volume expansion on the selected thin-provisioned volumes.
well-architect.oracle-tiering-policy-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends tiering FSx for ONTAP volumes used by databases when applicable. Tiering optimizes storage utilization by automatically moving less frequently accessed data such as snapshots or archived logs to cost-effective capacity tiers while keeping active data and redo logs on the high-performance primary storage tier. Tiering reduces overall storage costs, enhances performance for critical workloads, and simplifies management through automated data placement. For different Oracle files—data, redo log, and archive —distinct tiering policies ensure tailored efficiency.
well-architect.oracle-tiering-policy-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will enable tiering and configure the recommended FSx for ONTAP tiering policy based on the type of file that is located in the volume.
well-architect.oracle-tiering-min-cooling-days-action-s: Workload Factory recommends setting the appropriate minimum cooling days for a volume because it determines when data becomes eligible to move to cost-effective capacity tiers, optimizing storage costs while maintaining performance for frequently accessed data. Tailored settings for each volume type—data, redo log, and archive (FRA)—ensure efficient resource utilization.
well-architect.oracle-tiering-min-cooling-days-what-wil: Workload Factory will set the recommended minimum cooling days based on the type of file that is located in the volume.

Tailored settings for each volume type ensure alignment with Oracle’s I/O patterns: Data and archive Volumes benefit from inline adaptive compression (8KB), compaction and deduplication while Redo Log Volumes prioritize performance with minimal savings from these features.
well-architect.oracle-compression-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will set the recommended efficiency mechanisms based on the type of file that is located in the volume.

well-architect.oracle-space-reservation-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling space reservation on LUNs used by Oracle databases to reserve enough space in the volume so that writes to those LUNs don't fail.

well-architect.oracle-space-allocation-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling space allocation on LUNs used by Oracle databases to avoid write failures and inefficient space utilization. Space allocation ensures that FSx for ONTAP notifies the EC2 host when the volume is full and cannot accept writes. This setting also lets FSx for ONTAP  automatically reclaim space when the Oracle database on the EC2 host deletes data.

well-architect.oracle-swap-space-optimization-step4: Set proper permissions by running "sudo chmod 600 /swapfile".

well-architect.oracle-host-utility-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends installing host utilities for LUN and multipath management on systems hosting Oracle databases. These utilities ensure optimal compatibility, performance, and reliability when connecting to enterprise storage systems.
well-architect.oracle-host-utility-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will verify and, if necessary, install the required host utilities on the selected database host to ensure proper management of LUNs and multipath configurations.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-config-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends configuring the multipath configuration file with multipath defaults and blocked list settings as a NetApp best practice. This well-architected approach enables multipath I/O, ensures only intended storage devices are managed, improves reliability, prevents misconfiguration, and provides optimal performance and compatibility with ONTAP storage systems for Oracle databases.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-config-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will verify that the multipath configuration file (/etc/multipath.conf) is present and configured correctly with NetApp recommended settings on all relevant database hosts.
well-architect.oracle-transparent-hugepages-action-summ: Workload Factory recommends disabling Transparent HugePages (THP) on database hosts running Oracle databases. Disabling THP is an Oracle best practice to prevent potential performance issues and ensure optimal database stability.
well-architect.oracle-transparent-hugepages-what-will-h: Workload Factory will disable Transparent HugePages in the running system and configure the host to keep THP disabled after reboot.
well-architect.oracle-selinux-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends disabling SELinux on Oracle database hosts in the system configuration file. Disabling SELinux can help prevent potential compatibility issues with Oracle workloads and simplify system administration in environments where mandatory access controls are not required.
well-architect.oracle-selinux-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will update the SELinux configuration on the selected database host by setting 'setenforce 0'. It also changes the SELinux parameter from 'enforcing' to 'disabled' in /etc/selinux/config to ensure the change persists after a reboot.
well-architect.oracle-iscsi-replacement-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends reducing the iSCSI session replacement timeout value in the configuration file on Oracle database hosts. Lowering this timeout improves failover responsiveness in multipath environments, ensuring faster recovery from path failures.
well-architect.oracle-iscsi-replacement-what-will-happe: Workload Factory will update the iSCSI configuration on the selected database host by changing the node.session.timeo.replacement_timeout parameter from 120 to 5 seconds in /etc/iscsi/iscsid.conf. This change will enable the host to detect and recover from failed iSCSI paths more quickly, minimizing potential I/O disruptions. The iscsid service will be restarted to apply changes, and all services that use iSCSI may be impacted during this operation. However, database services are expected to remain uninterrupted due to multipath redundancy.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-friendly-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling the user_friendly_names parameter in the multipath configuration file for each Oracle database host. This provides clear, consistent naming for multipath devices, improving manageability and reducing the likelihood of errors during database and storage operations.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-friendly-what-will-happ: Workload Factory will verify and update the multipath configuration file on each database host to enable the user_friendly_names parameter. The multipathd daemon will be reloaded to apply changes, but this will not disrupt database services.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-io-sessions-action-summ: Workload Factory recommends configuring four Multipath I/O (MPIO) sessions for each Oracle database host using iSCSI connections to ONTAP storage. This ensures high availability and optimal performance by providing multiple redundant data paths between the server and storage.
well-architect.oracle-multipath-io-sessions-what-will-h: Workload Factory will verify and configure the database host to establish four active iSCSI sessions to the storage target, ensuring proper multipath redundancy and failover capability.
well-architect.oracle-multiblock-readcount-action-summa: Workload Factory recommends removing the db_file_multiblock_read_count parameter from the init.ora or (Server Parameter File) SPFILE file for Oracle databases. Leaving this parameter unset allows Oracle to automatically select the optimal value for sequential I/O performance.
well-architect.oracle-multiblock-readcount-what-will-ha: Workload Factory will check and remove any db_file_multiblock_read_count entry from the SPFILE or init.ora configuration file on the selected database host.
well-architect.oracle-filesystem-io-options-action-summ: Workload Factory recommends setting the Oracle filesystemio_options parameter to setall to enable both asynchronous and direct I/O for optimal database performance.
well-architect.oracle-filesystem-io-options-what-will-h: Workload Factory will set the Oracle initialization file to filesystemio_options = setall. If switching from buffered I/O, an increase in Oracle SGA memory may be required to compensate for the loss of OS buffer cache.

well-architect.oracle-tcp-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends enabling TCP timestamps, selective acknowledgment (SACK), and TCP window scaling on Oracle database hosts to ensure optimal network performance.
well-architect.oracle-tcp-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will verify and enable TCP timestamps, SACK, and window scaling in the host’s network configuration.
well-architect.oracle-afd-logical-block-size-action-sum: Workload Factory recommends configuring the Oracle ASM Filter Driver (AFD) to use the logical block size of the underlying FSx for ONTAP storage. This ensures that AFD aligns I/O operations with the storage’s block size, optimizing performance by minimizing latency and reducing unnecessary I/O overhead.

well-architect.oracle-afd-logical-block-size-note: It is crucial that you schedule this task during a maintenance window to minimize disruptions to your operations. This process could involve data loss and downtime. To prepare,  perform necessary backups and notify all affected users to avoid any unintended downtime or data loss.
well-architect.oracle-asmlib-logical-block-size-action-: Workload Factory recommends configuring Oracle ASMLib to use the logical block size of the underlying FSx for ONTAP storage, by setting the appropriate option in the ASMLib configuration file. This ensures that ASMLib aligns I/O operations with the storage’s block size, optimizing performance by minimizing latency and reducing unnecessary I/O overhead.
well-architect.oracle-asmlib-logical-block-size-what-wi: Workload Factory will add the logical block size alignment configuration to /etc/sysconfig/oracleasm file.

well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step2: Stop all database instances and listener services to free up current storage resources.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step3: Configure iSCSI LUNs as ASM disks for FSx for ONTAP, optionally labeling them with ASM Filter Driver or ASMLib for consistent access.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step4: Create ASM disk groups with external redundancy to utilize FSx for ONTAP built-in mirroring.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step5: Migrate database files (datafiles, redo logs, control files) to ASM disk groups using RMAN.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step6: Update Oracle configuration to use ASM disk groups (e.g., update control file paths).
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step7: Start the ASM instance, database, and listener, verifying full functionality.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step8: Verify database performance and FSx for ONTAP iSCSI integration with monitoring tools.
well-architect.oracle-asm-setup-optimization-step9: Remove the old file system or raw device storage after confirming the ASM setup works.
well-architect.oracle-asm-external-redundancy-action-su: Workload Factory recommends configuring Oracle ASM disk groups with EXTERNAL redundancy for FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs to leverage FSx for ONTAP's built-in high availability, optimize storage efficiency, and reduce costs by avoiding Oracle-level data mirroring.
well-architect.oracle-asm-external-redundancy-optimizat: Perform a full backup of the database to a separate location to ensure data recovery in case of issues.
Stop the database using the disk group (srvctl stop database -d <db_name>) to prevent access during migration.
Create a new ASM disk group with EXTERNAL redundancy using FSx for ONTAP iSCSI LUNs (e.g., CREATE DISKGROUP DATA_EXT EXTERNAL REDUNDANCY DISK '/dev/oracleafd/DATA01';).
Copy database files (datafiles, redo logs, control files) from the old mirrored disk group to the new EXTERNAL redundancy disk group.
Modify the database configuration (e.g., control_files, db_create_file_dest) to point to the new disk group.
Restart the database and verify functionality.
Once verified, drop the old mirrored disk group (DROP DISKGROUP DATA;) to free resources.
Confirm data integrity and performance using Automatic Workload Repository (AWR) reports and Amazon CloudWatch metrics (IOPS, latency <5ms) for FSx for ONTAP.

The nfs-rootonly setting for ONTAP restricts NFS connections to privileged ports (<1024). Since dNFS processes in NFSv4+ don't run as root and use higher ports, disabling this parameter allows necessary connections.

well-architect.oracle-export-policy-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends ensuring that the NFS export policy includes superuser and setuid permissions if Oracle binaries are located on the NFS share. Superuser (root) access allows NFS clients to map as root, which is needed for binary execution.

well-architect.oracle-export-policy-what-will-happen: Workload Factory will create a new similar export policy with the addition of 'superuser' and 'allow-suid' settings, and will assign this policy to the binaries volume.

well-architect.oracle-kernel-parameters-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends configuring the kernel parameters for the TCP slot table to 128 for Oracle workloads running on NFS. This configuration enables more concurrent I/O operations, reducing latency in high-throughput scenarios such as Oracle data file access. Kernel parameters govern the maximum number of outstanding NFS requests over TCP, acting like queue depth in Fibre Channel setups. The default Linux values, typically set at 16, are insufficient for optimal database performance.
well-architect.oracle-kernel-parameters-what-will-happe: Workload Factory will set the TCP slot table parameters to 128 in the /etc/sysctl.conf file.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-dbfiles-action-: Workload Factory recommends using optimized NFS mount options for database files. Key parameters include 'rw' for read/write access, 'bg' for background mounting, 'hard' for indefinite retries on failures, and 'proto=tcp' for reliable delivery. The 'rsize' and 'wsize' values of 262144 optimize large I/O operations, enhancing throughput, while 'nointr' ensures uninterrupted long-running tasks. This configuration is designed to improve database performance and resilience, particularly in high-throughput environments.

well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-dbfiles-step3: Edit the /etc/fstab file with recommended mount options.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-dbfiles-step4: Remount the file systems and restart the database.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-dbfiles-note: It is crucial that you schedule this task during a maintenance window to minimize disruptions to your operations. well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-adrhome-action-: Workload Factory recommends using optimized NFS mount options for the Automatic Diagnostic Repository (ADR) home, or root directory.  The Automatic Diagnostic Repository home stores logs and traces, which benefit from similar reliability options as core database files but don't require the nointr mount option since operations are less interrupt-sensitive.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-adrhome-what-wi: Workload Factory will do the following:
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-adrhome-step3: Edit the /etc/fstab file with recommended mount options.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-mount-options-adrhome-step4: Remount the file systems and restart the database.

well-architect.oracle-nfsv4-domain-name-action-summary: Workload Factory recommends ensuring the domain names in /etc/idmapd.conf on the host and NFS server (show -fields v4-id-domain in ONTAP) match for the NFSv4 protocol. The NFSv4 protocol uses string-based ID mapping (e.g., user@domain). Mismatches cause access denials.
well-architect.oracle-nfsv4-domain-name-user-action-req: Select the domain name > drop down with the found domain names
well-architect.oracle-nfsv4-domain-name-what-will-happe: Workload Factory will match the domain name in both locations based on the selected domain.

well-architect.oracle-nfs-caching-options-action-summar: Workload Factory recommends omitting NFS mount options that disable host caching—such as, 'actimeo=0' and 'noac'—in standalone Oracle deployments. These options are intended for use in clustered environments to ensure cache consistency, but in single-instance environments, they unnecessarily bypass caching and can significantly reduce performance. For optimal efficiency and reliability in standalone deployments, these options should not be present.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-caching-options-what-will-hap: Workload Factory will remount the file systems, removing the following mount options: cio, actimeo=0, noac, and forcedirectio.
well-architect.oracle-nfs-caching-options-note: It is crucial that you schedule this task during a maintenance window to minimize disruptions to your operations. well-architect.oracle-nfs-caching-optimization-step-3: Edit the /etc/fstab file to remove 'actimeo=0' and 'noac' options.

severity-description.0-9: Informational messages that return status information or report errors that aren't severe. The Database Engine doesn't raise system errors with severities of 0 through 9.
severity-description.10: Informational messages that return status information or report errors that aren't severe. For compatibility reasons, the Database Engine converts severity 10 to severity 0 before returning the error information to the calling application.
severity-description.11: Indicates that the given object or entity doesn't exist.
severity-description.12: A special severity for queries that don't use locking because of special query hints. In some cases, read operations performed by these statements could result in inconsistent data, since locks aren't taken to guarantee consistency.
severity-description.14: Indicates security-related errors, such as permission denied.
severity-description.15: Indicates syntax errors in the Transact-SQL command.
severity-description.16: Indicates general errors that can be corrected by the user.
severity-description.17: Indicates that the statement caused SQL Server to run out of resources (such as memory, locks, or disk space for the database) or to exceed some limit set by the system administrator.
severity-description.18: Indicates a problem in the Database Engine software, but the statement completes execution, and the connection to the instance of the Database Engine is maintained. The system administrator should be informed every time a message with a severity level of 18 occurs.
severity-description.19: Indicates that a nonconfigurable Database Engine limit has been exceeded and the current batch process has been terminated. Error messages with a severity level of 19 or higher stop the execution of the current batch. Severity level 19 errors are rare and must be corrected by the system administrator or your primary support provider. Contact your system administrator when a message with a severity level 19 is raised. Error messages with a severity level from 19 through 25 are written to the error log.
severity-description.20: Indicates that a statement has encountered a problem. Because the problem has affected only the current task, it is unlikely that the database itself has been damaged.
severity-description.21: Indicates that a problem has been encountered that affects all tasks in the current database, but it is unlikely that the database itself has been damaged.
severity-description.22: Indicates that the table or index specified in the message has been damaged by a software or hardware problem. Severity level 22 errors occur rarely. If one occurs, run DBCC CHECKDB to determine whether other objects in the database are also damaged. The problem might be in the buffer cache only and not on the disk itself. If so, restarting the instance of the Database Engine corrects the problem. To continue working, you must reconnect to the instance of the Database Engine; otherwise, use DBCC to repair the problem. In some cases, you may have to restore the database.If restarting the instance of the Database Engine doesn't correct the problem, then the problem is on the disk. Sometimes destroying the object specified in the error message can solve the problem. For example, if the message reports that the instance of the Database Engine has found a row with a length of 0 in a nonclustered index, delete the index and rebuild it.
severity-description.23: Indicates that the integrity of the entire database is in question because of a hardware or software problem.Severity level 23 errors occur rarely. If one occurs, run DBCC CHECKDB to determine the extent of the damage. The problem might be in the cache only and not on the disk itself. If so, restarting the instance of the Database Engine corrects the problem. To continue working, you must reconnect to the instance of the Database Engine; otherwise, use DBCC to repair the problem. In some cases, you may have to restore the database.
severity-description.24: Indicates a media failure. The system administrator may have to restore the database. You may also have to call your hardware vendor.
